# Guardrails Registry

This is the platform-wide policy registry for eq-sparks — the single, numbered list of every hard rule the harness operates under, from G1 to G15+. It is **enforced in three places, fail-fast**: **@critic** adjudicates at the review gate (strict PASS/FAIL on every agent's output), **@supervisor** holds the line at each stage gate (go/no-go, budget, and orchestrator barriers), and **hooks/CI** catch the mechanical rails at the pipeline (pre-commit/pre-edit hooks, branch protection, pipeline gates) before — and after — an agent ever reaches the gate. Each row names its **enforcing agent** and its **enforcement point**, so the cheapest mechanical check fires first and `opus`-tier judgment is spent only on what regex, path-matching, and branch protection cannot decide. The agent-level detail for the safety floor lives in [`safety-rails`](./safety-rails.md); this registry is the catalogue, `safety-rails` is the playbook.

**Enforcement-point classes** (the rightmost column):
- **Block action** — the offending action is refused inline; the agent halts and emits `BLOCKED:<reason>` to @supervisor. No budget or escalation buys past it.
- **Pipeline gate** — checked in CI/CD or by @infra at a deploy/quality gate; a failure stops the pipeline, not just one agent.
- **Code generation rule** — applied by the generating agent at write time and re-checked by @critic on the diff; a violation is an automatic @critic FAIL.
- **Code review check** — adjudicated by @critic (and/or @security) reading the diff at the review gate.
- **Pre-commit hook** — a mechanical hook fires before the change reaches history.
- **PR approval / branch protection** — enforced by the GitHub PR workflow; humans (and protection rules) gate the merge.

## G1–G14 — the platform floor

These are the non-negotiable platform rules. They are identical at every model tier; escalating from `haiku` to `sonnet` to `opus` does not unlock any of them, and no budget headroom buys past them.

- **G1 / G2 — Block action.** No agent may auto-merge a PR (G1) or touch a production config (G2). The action is refused inline and the agent emits `BLOCKED:guardrail` to @supervisor. G2 overlaps the `path-policy` denylist and the `no-build-config` rail in [`safety-rails`](./safety-rails.md).
- **G3 — Pipeline gate.** Security scans are never skipped; CI/CD and the orchestrators treat the scan stage as a hard gate. @scanner produces the scan; the orchestrator/CI refuses to advance without it.
- **G4 — Pre-commit hook.** A secret-pattern regex runs as a pre-commit/pre-edit hook so a credential never reaches disk or history; @scanner re-runs the same regex family across the diff as a Haiku-cheap backstop, and @critic FAILs on any hit. See `no-secrets` in [`safety-rails`](./safety-rails.md).
- **G5 — Code review check.** @codegen must never write PII into logs; @security reasons about the harder cases (structured logs, error payloads) and @critic adjudicates on the diff.
- **G6 — Report validation.** @scanner must never downgrade or suppress a vulnerability severity; the scan report is validated against the raw tool output, and a suppressed finding is a @critic FAIL.
- **G7 — Pipeline gate.** @infra blocks any deploy that has not passed all quality gates. @infra **reports — it never deploys**; it reads the active telemetry/observability sink and surfaces gate health to @supervisor and the console.
- **G8 — Code generation rule.** No synchronous DB calls — data access is async. Enforced by both @codegen (FE/BFF write-time) and @db (data-access correctness on the ExperienceAPI BFF), re-checked by @critic on the diff.
- **G9 — Code generation rule.** No string-concatenation SQL — queries are parameterised or go through the ORM. Same enforcers as G8 (@codegen + @db).
- **G10 — Code generation rule.** @codegen must never let a stack trace leak into an API response; error responses are sanitised at write time.
- **G11 — Code generation rule.** @codegen must never create an endpoint without auth attributes; an unauthenticated route is an automatic FAIL.
- **G12 — GitHub branch protection.** Minimum two reviewers; the PR workflow's branch-protection rules make a merge impossible without them. Mechanically enforced by GitHub, not by an agent.
- **G13 — Pipeline gate.** @infra blocks any PROD deploy lacking two human sign-offs. Two distinct sign-offs are a hard pipeline gate; @infra checks, never deploys.
- **G14 — PR-based approval.** @learner runs the curated-learning loop over cross-run telemetry and outcomes and **proposes** durable lessons into `shared/memory/lessons.md`, but **never auto-activates** a rule or lesson. Activation is a human merge of @learner's PR — proposes; humans merge. This is the path by which any G21+ rail is added to this registry.

## G15–G20 — EQ-specific rails

These encode the EQOne / ExperienceAPI house style on top of the platform floor. They are owned by the specialist agents named below and adjudicated by @critic at the review gate.

- **G15 — Code generation rule.** No duplicate code; anything common MUST move to `eq-one-shared`. Every build step runs the `dna-precheck` skill first (reuse / extend / create classification); @shared-curator owns the move-to-shared decision. Detail in [`dedup-policy`](./dedup-policy.md).
- **G16 — Code generation rule.** UI MUST use `eq-one-design-system` — never hand-rolled components. @design-system enforces; a bespoke control where a design-system primitive exists is a FAIL.
- **G17 — Pipeline gate.** The FE MUST match the ExperienceAPI contract; the build **fails on drift**. @contract runs the `contract-diff` skill against the published contract; drift stops the pipeline. Pairs with the BFF contract publisher path.
- **G18 — Code review check.** No dead code left behind — unreferenced exports, orphaned files, unreachable branches. @scanner detects; @shared-curator decides removal vs. move-to-shared; @critic confirms on the diff.
- **G19 — Code generation rule.** Respect MFE boundaries — no cross-microfrontend imports or boundary leaks. @mfe enforces at write time; a boundary crossing is a FAIL.
- **G20 — Code review check.** The BFF stays a BFF — no business logic in the experience layer. @domain-folder and @bff-shaper keep orchestration/shaping in the BFF and push business logic downstream; @critic adjudicates.

---

## How the three enforcement layers compose

The registry is enforced fail-fast so the cheapest, most mechanical check fires before expensive judgment:

1. **Hooks / CI (pipeline).** Pre-commit/pre-edit hooks (G4), the `path-policy` denylist (G2), GitHub branch protection (G12), and the deploy/quality gates @infra reads (G7, G13) all fire mechanically — before or independent of any LLM step. A failure here stops the change at the boundary.
2. **@supervisor (stage gate).** Between stages, @supervisor reconciles budget (`budget-check`), holds the orchestrator barriers, and makes the go/no-go. It aggregates every `BLOCKED:<reason>` and surfaces registry hits in the run Summary via `console-render`. @supervisor never relaxes a rail — it routes a forced fork to @decision and, where needed, to a human.
3. **@critic (review gate).** @critic owns the strict PASS/FAIL gate, checking each agent's output against this registry plus [`safety-rails`](./safety-rails.md). A hard-prohibition or code-generation-rule hit is a FAIL that blocks the stage until resolved.

A run can be cheap, deduplicated, and well-cached and still violate a guardrail — none of the optimisation policies ([`budget-policy`](./budget-policy.md), [`model-routing-policy`](./model-routing-policy.md), [`dedup-policy`](./dedup-policy.md), [`cache-policy`](./cache-policy.md)) can spend, escalate, or replay their way past a row in this table.

## Enforcing agents — cross-reference

| Agent | Owns / enforces |
|---|---|
| **@critic** | The review gate for the whole registry; strict PASS/FAIL on every diff. |
| **@supervisor** | Stage gates, go/no-go, budget barriers, Summary aggregation of all `BLOCKED:<reason>`. |
| **@infra** | G7, G13 — deploy/quality gates and PROD sign-offs; reads the telemetry/observability sink. Reports, never deploys. |
| **@db** | G8, G9 — data-access correctness on the ExperienceAPI BFF (async, parameterised/ORM, no N+1). |
| **@learner** | G14 — proposes durable lessons via PR; never auto-activates. The G21+ on-ramp. |
| **@scanner** | G3, G4 (backstop), G6, G18 — scans, secret backstop, severity integrity, dead-code detection. |
| **@security** | G5 — PII in logs and the harder authz/injection cases @critic relies on. |
| **@codegen** | G5, G8–G11 — write-time code-generation rules; G15/G16/G19 in concert with the specialists. |
| **@shared-curator** | G15, G18 — move-to-shared and dead-code removal (via `dna-precheck`). |
| **@design-system** | G16 — UI must use `eq-one-design-system`. |
| **@contract** | G17 — FE/contract drift via `contract-diff`. |
| **@mfe** | G19 — MFE boundary integrity. |
| **@domain-folder / @bff-shaper** | G20 — keep business logic out of the BFF. |

See [`safety-rails`](./safety-rails.md) for the agent-level hard-prohibition / soft-caution detail, and [`path-policy`](./path-policy.md) for the pre-tool-call filesystem enforcement behind G2.
